The endpoint must respond 200 and report either ok=false (SWI-Prolog rejected the file) OR ok=true but with a populated syntax_error field from the grammar parser. Either outcome confirms the checker ran without crashing.

test.doc: UFR-10: wrong code is identified by Shapiro's algorithm. WRONG_CODE has append([],Y,[]) instead of append([],Y,Y). The query append([a],[b],[a,b]) cleanly FAILS with the wrong base case (recursive call needs append([],[b],[b]) but the wrong clause only unifies to append([],[b],[]) → failure). Shapiro therefore classifies this as "incomplete" — the predicate is missing a clause that would make the goal succeed. Both "incomplete" and "incorrect" are non-ok bug indicators.
